claim: For A_k(n) = number of positive integers a such that a/n=1/m1+...+1/mk is solvable, the asymptotic bound x(log x)^3 << sum_{p<=x} A_3(p) << x(log x)^5 holds as x -> infinity, summing over primes p.
stance_target: asymptotic counting for three-term unit-fraction representability as a function of the denominator
scope_conditions: k=3, n=p prime, summed over primes p<=x
quoted_support: We show that x(log x)^3 << sum_{p<=x} A_3(p) << x(log x)^5 as x -> infinity.

claim: This paper counts, for each prime p, how many numerators a admit SOME three-term Egyptian fraction representation of a/p -- it does not address pairs of triples matched on both sum and reciprocal sum, so it is adjacent methodology rather than direct prior art for Section 5.
stance_target: prior art for Section 5's two-triple equal-sum-and-equal-reciprocal-sum problem
quoted_support: Given a positive integer n we let A_k(n) be the number of positive integers a such that a/n=1/m_1+1/m_2+...+1/m_k for some m_1,m_2,...,m_k in N.
